fact_rationales.F12: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome due to the underdeveloped left heart structures, which can lead to increased flow through the right heart and thus a louder systolic ejection murmur.
fact_rationales.F15: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is highly suggestive of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome, as this condition often results in increased blood flow to the lungs due to the underdevelopment of the left heart, leading to pulmonary overcirculation.

fact_rationales.F12: A single S2 and systolic ejection murmur can be seen in both atrial and ventricular septal defects, but the murmur is more characteristic of ventricular septal defects.
fact_rationales.F15: An enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is more commonly seen in ventricular septal defects due to increased flow through the pulmonary vasculature, but can also be seen in atrial septal defects.

fact_rationales.F12: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of truncus arteriosus due to the common arterial trunk, whereas tricuspid atresia would more likely present with different auscultation findings.
fact_rationales.F15: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is highly suggestive of truncus arteriosus due to excessive pulmonary blood flow, whereas tricuspid atresia might show decreased pulmonary vasculature.

fact_rationales.F12: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of truncus arteriosus due to the common arterial trunk, whereas tricuspid atresia would more likely present with different auscultation findings.
fact_rationales.F14: Bounding peripheral pulses are more characteristic of truncus arteriosus due to the direct connection between the aorta and pulmonary artery, leading to increased systemic blood flow, whereas tricuspid atresia would not typically present with this finding.
fact_rationales.F15: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is highly suggestive of truncus arteriosus due to the excessive pulmonary blood flow, making it less likely for tricuspid atresia which typically presents with decreased pulmonary blood flow.
fact_rationales.F9: Tachycardia is a nonspecific finding that can be present in both conditions due to distress or decreased cardiac output, thus it does not significantly differentiate between the two.

why.B1.1: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome is a possible explanation due to the underdeveloped left heart structures leading to increased flow through the right heart and thus a louder systolic ejection murmur, as well as the enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature.
why.B2.2: Ventricular Septal Defect could be considered due to the presence of a systolic ejection murmur and increased pulmonary vasculature, but it is less specific compared to Truncus Arteriosus and Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome.
why.B4.4: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur, along with enlarged cardiac silhouette and increased pulmonary vasculature, are highly suggestive of Truncus Arteriosus due to the common arterial trunk and excessive pulmonary blood flow.
